plugins.name: docs-sync
plugins.description: Pre-push code↔docs drift detection. Fans out Haiku searchers per code cluster, Sonnet editors per drifted page, then a Sonnet curator merges everything atomically into your push.

plugins.name: docs-create
plugins.description: End-to-end docs bootstrap: crawl a product URL with Haiku — or, when no source exists, research competitors and generate docs from a topic with Sonnet. Enrich with marketing pages (competitor vs, learn/, glossary, use-cases, migration guides), publish to GitHub, configure the Docsbook workspace via MCP. Unified positioning questions (problem + differentiator) across every route shape the README, AI chat prompt, and SEO meta. Guaranteed branding fallback chain in every crawler — no more colorless workspaces. One /docs-create command, five pinned subagents, two MCP servers (markdown-lsp + docsbook). Reads and writes Claude memory across runs so future sessions reuse the user's project context, competitor research, and style preferences.

plugins.name: docs-insights
plugins.description: Recurring analytics pipeline over the Docsbook MCP. Four pinned subagents (collector → clusterer → reporter → archivist) produce schema-validated JSON insight reports under .docsbook/insights/ on a configurable schedule. Designed so downstream actor agents can consume the JSON to drive Issues, edits, AI-chat tuning.

plugins.name: docs-audit
plugins.description: Full documentation quality audit, read-only. One pinned Sonnet auditor runs any of 17 checks — content types, structure, style, audience, navigation, SEO, accessibility, i18n, media, maintenance, trust, pricing consistency, competitor gap, rank recovery, title rewriting, content gaps, AI retrieval — and returns machine-readable JSON findings. Never edits a doc page; that is docs-sync's or docs-create's job.

plugins.name: docs-growth
plugins.description: Growth-reasoning pipeline over a product source-of-truth. Three pinned subagents (segment-analyst, funnel-analyst, competitor-analyst) reason about who buys, how they enter, and who competes — grounded in real analytics via docs-insights where data exists, simulated only where it cannot — and append what they learn back into the private knowledge base (about/, product-marketing context). Proposes and enriches; never touches product code or client docs. Emits schema-validated JSON for downstream opportunity-mapping or experiment-planning agents.
